frequency_question: How often does a central bank successfully complete the procedural sequence for a liquidity reserve ratio adjustment within a 105-day window when initiated?
membership_rule: Includes all documented instances where a central bank drafted, internally reviewed, legally vetted, and officially gazetted/notified a change in reserve ratios or incremental reserve ratios. Excludes general rate change cycles unless accompanied by specific reserve ratio directives.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major documented instances of reserve ratio adjustments by the RBI in the modern operating framework; all completed successfully well within the 105-day window once initiated.
known_gaps: Minor technical adjustments to exemptions or phased rollouts may exist in unindexed circulars, but major policy tool deployments are fully captured.
skeleton: Not applicable; direct enumeration of all major historical RBI reserve ratio instrument deployments meeting the procedural criteria.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 observed major historical instances where initiation led to completion within a short operational timeframe (<30 days).
validity_reason: Central bank operational frameworks, legal drafting protocols, and notification mechanisms evolve slowly over decades.
